<role>
You check one property (faithfulness) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is every claim in the brief supported by the cited evidence and the fact sheet, with nothing overstated and no cited contrary evidence left out? Pass means yes.
Fail on an uncited claim, a number that is off the fact sheet, a scope wider than the cited accounts, a paraphrase placed in quotation marks, or an ignored contrary citation.
The evidence is the brief, the cited insights and the fact sheet (accounts, ARR, mentions, routes, renewals).
</definition>

 "brief": "## Problem\n\nClaims handlers cannot process reserve adjustments when the primary approver is unavailable, because there is no backup approver or delegation mechanism. Reserve changes that exceed a handler's authority enter an approval waiting list and remain there until the specific approver returns, stalling claims indefinitely [i:655489deaf46b80c] [i:fe5045f877fd2a57]. This delay blocks downstream activity including payments and reporting [i:d25753b53cd1ed5f].\n\n## Who is affected\n\n- Callowfield Auto Assurance, where claims are held up because the approver is out and there is no backup, causing the approval waiting list to pile up [i:17d1c301c6216534].\n- Wexmoor Motor, where claims are stuck because reserve changes need approval but no one is covering for the approver [i:4da72a0298cc1806].\n- Holloway Reach Underwriting, where reserve adjustments above the team's limit sit until the approver comes back, with no backup and no delegation [i:62370a71c63f0356].\n- Ravensgill Insurance, where a reserve adjustment beyond a handler's limit goes into an approval waiting list and nothing moves if the approver is out [i:655489deaf46b80c].\n- Harrowfield Fleet Mutual, where a reserve exceeding authority with the approver out and no delegate piles up on the approval waiting list [i:981bdf2d38caaa15].\n- Pendleford Motor Mutual, where reserve changes wait for an approver on leave with no delegate set up [i:a220bdb07381e46e].\n- Saltmarsh Specialty, where reserve updates beyond handler limits are stuck waiting for sign-off with no backup approver, halting payments and reporting [i:d25753b53cd1ed5f].\n- Sallowmere Motor, which asked to review the roles assigned to its claims handlers because some tasks are getting stuck in the queue [i:293889b99ef6cf16].\n\n## Evidence\n\n- Across 8 accounts, there are 18 mentions of this problem, arriving via 3 routes: 7 via support, 6 via sales and 5 via account management [i:17d1c301c6216534] [i:293889b99ef6cf16] [i:981bdf2d38caaa15]. Total ARR across the accounts listed is £5420000.0, and there are 0 renewals in the next 90 days [i:17d1c301c6216534].\n- Callowfield Auto Assurance (ARR £1250000.0, renewal 2027-03-31) raised 4 mentions, including that claims are held up because the approver is out and there is no backup [i:17d1c301c6216534], and that when a reserve change goes beyond what a handler can approve, it just sits there [i:47e4aac56f39b4d3].\n- Wexmoor Motor (ARR £1950000.0, renewal 2027-06-30) raised 3 mentions, including that the reserve authorisation delay blocks everything until the approver returns [i:b4704c93f5c948f7] and that nothing moves when a handler tries to adjust a reserve beyond their limit and the approver is out of office with no delegate assigned [i:fe5045f877fd2a57].\n- Holloway Reach Underwriting (ARR £320000.0, renewal 2027-08-22) raised 2 mentions, including that the approval waiting list is the big blocker [i:eef547df758f4ba9].\n- Ravensgill Insurance (ARR £470000.0, renewal 2027-04-30) raised 2 mentions, including that when a handler needs to adjust a reserve beyond their limit, it goes into an approval waiting list and nothing moves until the approver returns [i:96e26adc2310c91f].\n- Harrowfield Fleet Mutual raised 1 mention, that when a reserve exceeds authority and the approver is out with no delegate, it piles up and causes unnecessary delays [i:981bdf2d38caaa15].\n- Pendleford Motor Mutual (ARR £690000.0, renewal 2027-02-28) raised 2 mentions, including that the approval waiting list just sits there if the approver is out [i:c982d8e917d59cce].\n- Saltmarsh Specialty (ARR £740000.0, renewal 2027-05-15) raised 3 mentions, including that there is no delegate at all, causing delays on reserve updates that need sign-off before payments can be processed [i:b9562428ce218966].\n- Sallowmere Motor raised 1 mention, asking to review the roles assigned to its claims handlers because some tasks are getting stuck in the queue [i:293889b99ef6cf16].\n\n## Why now\n\n- The problem is reported across 8 accounts and 18 mentions, spanning 3 routes (7 support, 6 sales, 5 account management), with total ARR of £5420000.0 across the accounts listed [i:17d1c301c6216534] [i:293889b99ef6cf16] [i:981bdf2d38caaa15].\n- There are 0 renewals in the next 90 days, so no renewal is immediately at risk, but the earliest renewal dates in the fact sheet fall in 2027, including Pendleford Motor Mutual on 2027-02-28 and Callowfield Auto Assurance on 2027-03-31 [i:c982d8e917d59cce] [i:17d1c301c6216534].\n- The cited insights consistently describe the same mechanism: reserve changes beyond handler authority enter an approval waiting list with no backup approver, and nothing moves until the approver returns [i:655489deaf46b80c] [i:fe5045f877fd2a57] [i:a220bdb07381e46e].\n- The impact extends beyond queue delay: Saltmarsh Specialty reports that the reserve authorisation delay halts payments and reporting [i:d25753b53cd1ed5f], and Callowfield Auto Assurance describes the situation as not sustainable [i:f6dc3676926959e6].",

response.content: {"critique": "I checked the aggregate figures (8 accounts, 18 mentions, routes 7 support / 6 sales / 5 account management, ARR £5,420,000, 0 renewals in 90 days) against the fact sheet and they all match exactly. Per-account details (ARR, renewal dates, mention counts) also match, and accounts with null ARR/renewal (Sallowmere, Harrowfield) are correctly listed without those figures. Each account claim is supported by a cited insight whose quote matches the paraphrase, including the Sallowmere role-review request and the Saltmarsh payments/reporting impact; no paraphrases are placed in quotation marks and no contrary evidence is present. The 'stalling claims indefinitely' phrasing is a mild rhetorical extension but is grounded in the cited 'nothing moves until the approver returns' language.", "verdict": "pass"}
